title: run_profile
description: Machine-readable IR of a generated UVM environment's single authoritative execution surface (its Makefile, or an SoC-level reference command.txt). An agent must never compose a vcs/simv command line from scratch or from a paraphrase of documentation -- it may only invoke the params/targets listed here, exactly as reverse-derived from the real source file named in `source`. A knob an agent believes is missing goes to the question queue; it is never silently added here by an agent.

kind.description: makefile: a Make-based build/run driver (this harness's own generated IP-level UVM environments). command_txt: an SoC-level reference command.txt whose SystemVerilog tasks are the sole authority for a SYSTEM_LEVEL_MODE environment's execution method. Both kinds normalize into the same fields below.

path.description: Path to the real source file this profile was extracted from, relative to the environment root.

content_sha256.description: Hash of the source file at extraction time, so a stale run_profile.json (source changed since) can be detected before an agent trusts it.

target_ip.description: Upper-case protocol name, e.g. USB, PCIE, MIPI_CSI. Matches TARGET_IP.

ip_prefix.description: Lower-case file/class prefix with trailing underscore. Matches IP_PREFIX.

extra_tops.description: Modules referenced by bare name but never instantiated, so VCS drops them unless named as extra elaboration tops. Matches EXTRA_TOPS. Never guessed -- only ever populated from a real Error-[XMRE]/Error-[NTMES] evidence trail, same discipline as the reference Makefile's own comment for this field.

required_paths.description: Paths the source file's own consistency-check block $(error)s on if unset or malformed. Order carries no meaning; `required` distinguishes a hard stop from an optional/defaulted path.

must_contain.description: Sibling files/directories the source's own tree-integrity check requires directly under this path (e.g. DUT_ROOT_PATH needing MACRO/MODEL/ENV/DUMMY_TOP/RTLCAT).

compile_time_params.description: Knobs that select DUT/VIP configuration and require a rebuild to take effect. An agent must treat a change to any of these as invalidating the current simv.

runtime_params.description: Knobs applied as run-time plusargs; changing one costs one simulation, never a rebuild.

defines.description: Compile-time +define+ macros, unconditional or gated behind a compile_time_param.

controlled_by.description: Name of the compile_time_param whose value gates this define.

when.description: The controlling param value that turns this define on.

compile_flags.description: Fixed (non-user-overridable) flag groups the source always passes to vlogan/vcs -- bitmode, NTB/Vera compatibility, VIP/TB incdirs, VIP interface-width macros. Captured verbatim so a justfile/agent never has to reconstruct them by reading the VIP examples again.

enabled_by.description: Var name that switches local vs LSF-batch execution, e.g. LSF.

path.description: Registry file mapping a PATTERN/scenario name to its directory, e.g. tb/patterns/pattern_list.txt.

selector_param.description: Name of the runtime_params entry that selects a registry row, e.g. PATTERN.

constraints.description: Cross-field validity rules reverse-derived from the source's own $(error)/$(warning) guard blocks. Every rule here MUST be checked before invoking the underlying make/run command -- this is what lets a justfile recipe fail fast with the source's own actionable message instead of vcs failing silently or thousands of lines deep.

kind.description: enum_membership: field value must be in the field's own enum (redundant safety net, already expressible via param.enum, kept when the guard names extra invalid-looking-but-plausible values e.g. 'gen3'). mutual_requirement: fields A implies B must satisfy some condition. forbidden_combination: named combination is rejected outright. retired: the param itself is a hard error now, never a no-op.

message.description: Verbatim (or lightly trimmed) $(error) text -- this is what surfaces to the agent/user, not a paraphrase.

targets.description: The only verbs an agent may invoke. Each corresponds 1:1 to a real make target / command.txt entry point.

name.description: e.g. compile, sim, regress, check, help, clean, list_patterns.

params.description: Subset of compile_time_params/runtime_params names this target actually reads. An agent passing a param not listed here for this target is a sign it is guessing, not reading the profile.

plusarg.description: The literal +NAME= or +NAME token forwarded at run time, when different from the bare var name (e.g. TEST -> +UVM_TESTNAME=).

per_instance_of.description: If set, this param is the per-instance override family root (e.g. SPEED -> SPEED0/SPEED1 exist as siblings with the same enum, defaulting to this param's value).
